comparison: Perfect agreement on RNA-seq methodology and rhythmic transcript identification (C2, C40-C44, C46). Both evaluations find the technical approaches appropriate and well-supported, with OpenEval highlighting specific methodological strengths (Gaussian mixture model, dual algorithm approach) and peer reviewers affirming the RNA-seq and analysis methods as 'solid support for data interpretation.'

Strong agreement on GO enrichment analysis (C3, C57, C58). Both evaluations support the findings without challenge. OpenEval notes the appropriate exclusion of core clock genes, while peer reviewers accept the identification of Ca2+ homeostasis as rhythmic and describe the work as 'important' for highlighting circadian rhythms in astrocytes.

Agreement on Herp rhythmicity validation (C4, C59-C63, C67-C69), though peer review R3 also includes Bmal1-/- data (C5, C70-C72) that OpenEval separates into R4. Both evaluations affirm the multi-method validation approach and technical rigor. Peer reviewers note the manuscript was 'considerably improved with experiments and more solid data analysis.'

Partial overlap on Bmal1-/- validation (C5, C70-C72). OpenEval R4 focuses specifically on genetic evidence for circadian control, while peer R3 groups this with the broader Herp rhythmicity findings. Both evaluations support the use of Bmal1-/- astrocytes as appropriate genetic validation.

Strong agreement on HERP-ITPR mechanistic findings (C6, C80-C82, C85-C88). Both evaluations affirm the siRNA knockdown and Ca2+ imaging approaches. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of compartment-specific indicators and pharmacological validation, while peer reviewers explicitly state 'siRNA, Ca2+ imaging' provide 'solid support for data interpretation.'

Agreement on circadian phase-dependent Ca2+ responses (C7, C89-C90, C92-C95). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval details the logic connecting rhythmic ITPR2 to the observed effects, while peer reviewers state the study 'provides significant insights into how the circadian clock influences astrocytic Ca2+ homeostasis.'

Both address differential ITPR regulation (C8), though peer R5 groups this with broader circadian Ca2+ findings (C7, C9, C89-C95). OpenEval notes the mechanistic explanation is supported but leaves questions for future work. Peer reviewers accept the findings as part of the 'appropriate' technical approaches without specific concerns.

Perfect agreement on Bmal1-/- Ca2+ dynamics validation (C96-C99). Both evaluations support the genetic evidence. OpenEval emphasizes the mechanistic consistency between constant low HERP and faster Ca2+ release, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the 'appropriate' technical approaches that 'strengthened the conclusions.'

Strong agreement on CX43 phosphorylation findings (C10, C103-C104, C106-C107). Both evaluations support the connexin data. OpenEval highlights HERP as a critical intermediate in the pathway, while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the overall mechanistic story providing 'significant insights.'

Both address in vivo validation (C105). OpenEval supports the finding but notes limitation of only two time points. Peer R7 groups this with broader CX43 findings and accepts it as part of 'appropriate' technical approaches, though one reviewer elsewhere cautions about in vivo extrapolations.

Perfect agreement on gap junction functional measurements (C11, C108-C111, C141). Both evaluations support the gap-FRAP methodology and findings. OpenEval details the CBX control validation and consistency with known CX43 phosphorylation effects, while peer reviewers describe the approaches as 'appropriate' with 'solid' data analysis.

Significant disagreement on broader functional implications (C12, C139-C140, C145-C146). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model is logical but speculative without direct measurement of synaptic activity. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN but more critically, with one explicitly stating 'all references to the in vivo situation are speculative and should be absolutely avoided' for this in vitro work.

OpenEval evaluates direct transcriptional regulation evidence (C118-C121) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of experimental validation of E-boxes. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these bioinformatic claims about HERP promoter regulation.

OpenEval evaluates the negative mitochondrial Ca2+ result (C91, C130-C136) as SUPPORTED, praising the authors' thoughtful speculation and appropriate caution. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these mitochondrial findings.

OpenEval evaluates CircaDB comparative analysis (C47-C51, C54-C55) as SUPPORTED, noting sound methodology and interesting tissue-specific findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this comparative database analysis.

OpenEval evaluates contextualization with sleep/wake literature (C137-C138, C147-C151) as SUPPORTED, praising balanced interpretation of supporting and conflicting findings. Peer R9 touches on C151 but focuses on broader speculation concerns rather than literature contextualization.

Both address speculation about SCN astrocytes (C124). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the connection is plausible but requires direct testing. Peer R10 also rates UNCERTAIN, with one reviewer explicitly cautioning that 'references to the in vivo situation are speculative' for this in vitro work.

Both address summary statements about study significance (C152-C154). OpenEval supports these as fair characterizations of the work's contributions. Peer R9 acknowledges the work is 'important' and 'timely' but cautions about extrapolations beyond in vitro findings, creating tension with broader claims.
